headline: Food Trucks Are Only the Beginning of Mobile Hospitality
deck: Boats, trailers, pop-ups, concessions and mobile kitchens all force the same question: can the operation actually work in the space you have?
author: Josh Freeman
heroImageAlt: Cook working inside a food truck kitchen
body: The interesting part of mobile hospitality is not the truck. It is the constraint.

A boat galley, food trailer, festival booth and mobile bar all make operators solve space, power, water, storage, holding, service speed and menu complexity in a tighter environment than a normal restaurant.

That is why the concept should come before the equipment list. Start with what you are selling, how many people you need to serve and what absolutely has to happen during service. Then build the mobile operation backward from that.
joshTake: A cool truck with the wrong menu and utilities is still the wrong business. I would design the service before I shop for the toys.
